State of Missouri Shares New Details on Planned Detonation at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant 

November 24, 2026

Jefferson City

The State of Missouri is sharing new information ahead of tomorrow’s controlled detonation of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. This federal operation is intended to reduce the risk of an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion and is still expected to have minimal impact on portions of northeast Missouri.
The federal multi-agency team planning the detonation is taking unprecedented measures to both contain the explosion and limit the dispersion of lead into the environment. These efforts include layers of earth, sand, water and two feet of high-expansion foam in addition to the concrete bunker in which the detonation will occur. 
Because of these mitigation measures, and the fact that the Missouri state line is 57 miles from the IAAAP, impacts are expected to be extremely limited for communities in Missouri. 
“Keeping Missourians safe means keeping Missourians informed with facts,” said 
Governor Kehoe
. “While risk to Missourians remains minimal, our State Emergency Operations Center is activated and our state agencies continue to be in constant contact with federal partners to take the necessary actions to protect the health and safety of our citizens, livestock, and environment.”
The U.S. Army today released its first 
dispersion modeling map
 for the planned detonation. The models indicate anticipated lead levels will be within acceptable standards for both surfaces and ambient air. The first map shows the distribution of dust and the potential lead concentration that is anticipated from the event. The second map shows estimated airborne concentrations as the airmass travels over the ground surface during the day.
Based upon this information, the Missouri Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services (DHSS) continue to believe this event does not pose a serious threat to Missouri’s environment or public health. For additional context, the concentration of lead that Missourians may be exposed to during this short-term event is a fraction of the Permissible Exposure Limit allowed by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) for Missourians working in general industry and construction.
The U.S. Army will continue to update the maps on the 
Iowa Army Ammunition Plant website
 based on the latest weather forecasts.  
Although the state does not anticipate a serious health risk for Missourians, constituents looking for official information, health guidance, and links to resources from state and federal agencies should visit the 
Missouri Department of Natural Resources' webpage
. Updates will continue to be made to the webpage prior to and following the detonation.
